subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: From which French word does the term 'collage' derive?
questions.explain: Collage comes from the French verb 'coller', meaning to stick or glue materials onto a surface.

questions.q: Media such as ink, watercolour and acrylic paint are described as which type of media?
questions.explain: Wet media are fluid materials such as paints and inks that are applied in a liquid state.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a dry medium?
questions.explain: Charcoal is a dry medium, along with graphite pencil and soft pastel.

questions.q: What is the term for an image constructed by combining and arranging cut or torn photographs?
questions.explain: Photomontage is the technique of assembling a composite image from multiple photographic pieces.

questions.q: Which technique involves placing paper over a textured surface and rubbing with a pencil or crayon to capture the texture?
questions.explain: Frottage records surface texture by rubbing a drawing medium over paper laid on a textured object.

questions.q: Which adhesive is most commonly used to stick papers when making a collage?
questions.explain: PVA glue is a versatile, water-based adhesive widely used to attach collage materials.

questions.q: Which two artists are widely credited with pioneering collage (papier collé) in the early 20th century?
questions.explain: Picasso and Braque introduced papier collé around 1912 as part of their Cubist experiments.

questions.q: What is the purpose of applying fixative to a charcoal or pastel drawing?
options: To stop the medium smudging and hold it in place
To add a glossy varnish layer
questions.explain: Fixative binds loose dry pigment to the surface so the drawing does not smudge.

questions.q: Why might an artist apply a layer of gesso to a surface before working on it?
options: To prime and prepare the surface so media adhere well
To dissolve any glue used earlier
To speed up the drying of watercolour
questions.explain: Gesso primes a support, creating a stable, slightly textured ground that helps media grip.

questions.q: What visual effect is created by layering translucent or semi-transparent media over one another?
options: Underlying colours and marks show through, creating depth
The surface becomes completely opaque and flat
All texture is removed from the work
questions.explain: Translucent layers allow lower layers to remain partly visible, building a sense of depth and richness.

questions.q: Why does a wax crayon act as a resist when a water-based wash is painted over it?
options: The wax repels the water-based paint so the marks show through
The wax dissolves and mixes into the paint
The wax absorbs the water, darkening the paint
The wax changes the paint's colour chemically
questions.explain: Wax is water-repellent, so a wash slides off the waxed marks and settles only on the bare paper.

questions.q: What is a key reason for combining different media within a single piece of work?
options: To create varied texture, surface and visual interest
To make the work quicker and cheaper only
To ensure the work uses no colour
To avoid having to develop any ideas
questions.explain: Combining media exploits the contrasting qualities of each material to enrich texture and effect.

questions.q: The technique of 'sgraffito' involves which action?
options: Scratching through a top layer to reveal a colour beneath
Gluing torn paper into overlapping layers
Rubbing a pencil over a textured object
Building paint up thickly with a knife
questions.explain: Sgraffito exposes an underlayer by scratching lines into a surface layer above it.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of keeping a sketchbook when working with mixed media?
options: To record, explore and develop ideas as they progress
To store finished pieces for display only
To copy other artists' finished work exactly
questions.explain: A sketchbook documents the evolution of ideas, experiments and refinements throughout a project.

questions.q: In art coursework, what is a 'primary source'?
options: Something observed or recorded first-hand by the artist
An image copied from a book or website
A piece made entirely by another artist
A colour chart supplied by a manufacturer
questions.explain: Primary sources are gathered directly from firsthand observation, such as your own photographs or drawings from life.

questions.q: Why is it usually sensible to allow a wet layer such as an acrylic wash to dry before adding fine ink line work on top?
options: So the ink sits crisply on a stable surface rather than bleeding
Because ink cannot be used with acrylic at all
So the wash lifts off completely
To make the ink change colour
questions.explain: A dry underlayer stops the ink spreading, keeping line work sharp and controlled.

questions.q: What does annotating your studies in a sketchbook help you to do?
options: Explain your thinking, choices and how ideas are developing
Hide your working from the examiner
Replace the need for any images
Guarantee a higher mark without any artwork
questions.explain: Annotation makes your creative decisions and development of ideas explicit and visible.

questions.q: A student wants to build up an image using overlapping torn papers, fabric and printed text with a strong sense of depth. Which approach best suits this?
questions.explain: Layered collage of assorted materials directly creates overlapping surfaces and depth.

questions.q: A student needs to capture the rough texture of tree bark quickly and directly to use in a mixed-media piece. Which technique is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Frottage transfers a real surface texture straight onto paper by rubbing over it.

questions.q: Having produced several media experiments, a student now wants to show how their idea evolves towards a final outcome. What should they do in their sketchbook?
options: Record and develop the idea through progressive studies and annotation
Glue in only the finished piece with no notes
Leave the pages blank to save space
questions.explain: Progressive annotated studies evidence the recording and development of ideas towards a resolved outcome.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Art and Design specifications; Mixed Media
